prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1282; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by phone today. Insured states a vehicle was struck while parked in a store parking lot and the other driver left the scene before exchanging details.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured's household driver, who was operating the vehicle at the time. The account matches the initial report, and the driver says a bumper was pushed in on the rear passenger side.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report reference. Officers attended the lot and recorded the statements of two witnesses who saw the collision and confirmed the claimant was seated in the vehicle when it happened.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the insured's phone were received. The damage shown on the rear quarter panel and bumper is consistent with the impact described by everyone so far.

Entry 5: Claimant is now represented by counsel. All future contact will go through the attorney's office, and a letter of representation has been placed in the file.

Entry 6: Counsel's office sent a demand package listing neck and lower back complaints. Records requested from the first treating provider; it is not yet clear whether the back injury stems from this crash or from another source.

Entry 7: Reviewed the treatment records. Care followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication, and symptoms eased steadily as the claimant improved. No earlier injury to the same body area appears in the records we have.

Entry 8: Spoke with the other driver, who independently confirmed the sequence of events and the position of both vehicles. Nothing in that account conflicts with the physical damage or the witness statements.

Entry 9: Vehicle inspected at the repair facility. Estimator found no earlier damage to the vehicle and no prior repair records surfaced in the database check. The findings line up with the described impact.

Entry 10: Confirmed the policy was active on the date of loss and that the driver is a household member of the policyholder and therefore covered. Nothing points to any damage occurring before coverage began.

Entry 11: Counsel was asked for prior medical history and wage documentation. Claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation to date, and no inconsistencies have been noted.

Entry 12: Injury evaluation remains open pending the treating doctor's final note and the records review. Reserves are being kept at the current level until the medical causation question is resolved.
